info.title: Loyverse API
info.description:
# Using the REST API
The Loyverse API follows the general patterns of REST. You can use the resources of a Loyverse account (items, receipts, etc.) by making HTTPS requests to URLs that represent those resources. You can find description of all the endpoints here.

To test and explore Loyverse API you can use Postman. Postman is a powerful HTTP client for testing RESTful APIs by displaying requests and responses in manageable formats.

These are steps you need to take to start testing Loyverse API via Postman:
1. Download and install Postman. You can get it here: [https://www.getpostman.com](https://www.getpostman.com)

2. Get [Loyverse API Postman Collection](https://developer.loyverse.com/docs/Loyverse_API.postman_collection.json) and import it into Postman.

3. Define variables used in postman collection. For example, in Loyverse production environment for Loyverse API v1.0 you should define `baseUrl` variable as `https://api.loyverse.com/v1.0`. It is useful to configure variables in postman environments so you will not have to redefine the values for each request manually. [Learn more about Postman environments](https://learning.postman.com/docs/sending-requests/managing-environments/)

4. Configure the Postman Authorization header. Each request to Loyverse API should contain a token in request header. You can read more about ways to get the token in the Authorization section of the documentation.

Once you complete these steps you are ready to make calls to Loyverse API via Postman.



# Versioning

The Loyverse API uses versioning. This documentation is for version 1.0 of the API. Version must be specified in the base URL, for example: `https://api.loyverse.com/v1.0`

# Authorization

An application credential is any piece of information that identifies, authenticates, or authorizes an application in some way.

Loyverse API provide two authorization methods:
* Personal access tokens
* OAuth 2.0
## Personal access tokens
Personal access tokens are a simple way to make calls to the API. This authorization method suites best e.g. for periodically running scripts on data of your own account.

You can get your personal access token on the [corresponding page](https://r.loyverse.com/dashboard/#/integrations/tokens) in the back office of your account. For every call to the API you must include your access token in the Authorization header:

```
{
  Authorization: Bearer fMYgxHEYtcyT8cvtvgi1Za5DRs4vArSyvydlnd9f
}
```

Be aware that personal access token gives unlimited access to the targeted account.
## OAuth 2.0
The main steps of OAuth flow are:
1. Creating your app
2. Requesting a temporary authorization code
3. Requesting an access token
4. Making API requests
5. Refreshing the access token as needed

### Creating an application
To create an app go to the [developer dashboard](http://developer.loyverse.com/apps) and specify all required data for your app. After  successfully creating your app you will be given a set of 2 unique keys `client_id` and `client_secret` which are used to identify your app and are required to complete the authorization process.
### OAuth Authentication Flow
The merchant (resource owner) needs to authorize your app to access their data. Guide them to the authorization URL so that they can authorize your app. Authorization URL must be in format:

```
https://api.loyverse.com/oauth/authorize?client_id={client_id}&scope={scope}&response_type=code&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}&state={state}
```

This URL must contain query parameters:
* client_id: the app id provided when creating your app.
* response_type: specify ‘code’ that means your app is requesting an authorization code grant.
* redirect_uri: should be equal to one of the redirect URL list provided when creating your app.
* scope: the list of permissions to the retailer's account that you app needs (the complete list of permissions see below). The scope values must be separated with the space character, %20.
* state: a random value provided by your app that is unique for each authorization request. It is used to link requests and callbacks to  prevent cross-site request forgery attacks. During the OAuth callback, your app must check that this value matches the one you provided during authorization.

**Permissions list:**

Permission | Description
----------|-------------
CUSTOMERS_READ | Read customer information
CUSTOMERS_WRITE | Edit customer information
EMPLOYEES_READ | Read employee information
ITEMS_READ | Read items, categories, discounts and modifiers
INVENTORY_READ | Read inventory
INVENTORY_WRITE | Edit inventory 
ITEMS_WRITE | Edit items, discounts, categories and modifiers
MERCHANT_READ | Read merchant information
PAYMENT_TYPES_READ | Read payment types
POS_DEVICES_READ | Read POS devices information
POS_DEVICES_WRITE | Update POS devices information
RECEIPTS_READ | Read receipts
RECEIPTS_WRITE | Create receipts
SHIFTS_READ | Read shifts
STORES_READ | Read store information
SUPPLIERS_READ | Read supplier information
SUPPLIERS_WRITE | Edit supplier information
TAXES_READ | Read taxes
TAXES_WRITE | Edit taxes


Once directed to this link, the merchant will be asked to log in to their Loyverse account (if he is not already logged in). He will then be asked to allow or deny the authentication request. After allowing access, an authorization code will be sent back to your app to the specified redirect URI.

Once you have the authorization code, your app can now request an access token by sending a request to the following Access Token URL:

```
https://api.loyverse.com/oauth/token
```

The payload of your request must be with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded and include:
* client_id
* client_secret
* redirect_uri
* code
* grant_type (specify ‘authorization_code’)

In case of successful request you will get a response with an access token.  Response example:

```
{
  "access_token": "39557133-8881-4ce7-99b5-2ab4d15c2092",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 43200,
  "refresh_token": "J3F62YPIQdfJjJia1xJuaHp7NoQYtm9y0WadNBTh",
  "scope": "ITEMS_READ"
}
```

Once you receive an access token you can use it to interact with the Loyverse API on behalf of the merchant by providing the access token in an Authorization header.

### Refreshing access token

When the access token expires you can obtain a new one by making POST request to `https://api.loyverse.com/oauth/token` with the following parameters:

* client_id
* client_secret
* refresh_token
* grant_type (specify "refresh_token")


## OpenID Connect 
[OpenID Connect](https://openid.net/connect/) is a simple identity layer on top of the OAuth 2.0 protocol. It allows your app to authorize the user and obtain basic user profile information.

ID token is a [JSON Web Token (JWT)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7519) that contains identity information about the user that is digitally signed by Loyverse. To get ID token you need to specify `OPENID` scope in the authorization request along with other scopes that are necessary for your app.

Response example: 
```
{
  "access_token": "39557133-8881-4ce7-99b5-2ab4d15c2092",
  "id_token": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9..n2wQZtRRU0k2bGxSaz9BY6blf8dAXDAG47UBbAiW9vH8YVnZ1CBcvxkzARAUDjTGuZbGLLUFvzHLT8X5DPulXUt8LhZS2YOpnJccVWrH8RiatwAErwmGGkxJisPwJrFVgQ0qX0O2Wo3NiA_UfY9g3SSveexfOE6g2VWTct8eMdzB0qTyBrtIPtBSVXApdSxF1d5Abl8e2xu2R5LDTdQhb4YxzLejU-sU9ppdYedJBqorhzJBfs6Mi7YyzsCGQ5SrY1ZA7pQNHuO9bUijyj3pHMshlcpvZJzxOfYbEczyUKMsQPdlqdgHGlyaoYJhQuVKPVxVz06dpBBpsdwMfI6Ofw"
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 43200,
  "refresh_token": "J3F62YPIQdfJjJia1xJuaHp7NoQYtm9y0WadNBTh",
  "scope": "OPENID ITEMS_READ ITEMS_WRITE RECEIPTS_READ"
}
```

An ID token consists of three encoded parts separated by dots:
* Header
* Payload
* Signature

Header is Base64Url encoded JSON with the following structure:
```
{
  typ: "JWT",
  alg: "RS256"
}
```
* typ: the type of the token
* alg: the hashing algorithm being used, such as HMAC SHA256 or RSA

The second part of ID token is a payload that has metadata about the user. Loyverse provides following fields (claims):

Claim|Description
----------|-------------
aud | The audience that this ID token is intended for. It must be the OAuth 2.0 client ID of a developer app.
exp | The time when ID token expires, represented in Unix time (integer seconds).
iat | The time the ID token was issued. Represented in Unix time (integer seconds).
iss | The issuer identifier for the issuer of the response. This is always set to https://api.loyverse.com
sub | An identifier for the user, unique among all Loyverse accounts and never reused. You can use sub within your application as the unique-identifier key for the user.
country | The country code associated with the merchant account (ISO 3166-1-alpha-2 format)
name | The name of business
email | The account email address
created_at | The date and time when the merchant account was created

The payload example:
```
{
  "sub": "b4d08058-dc81-11ea-90b4-1269e7c5a22d",
  "aud": "rmCfGKJJ22UdUGndankJ",
  "iss": "https://api.loyverse.com",
  "iat": 1353601026,
  "exp": 1353604926,
  "country": "jp",
  "name": "Best Store",
  "created_at": "2020-06-04T15:44:20.020+03:00",
  "email": "jsmith@example.com",
}
```
The same info you can get by calling `https://api.loyverse.com/userinfo` endpoint.
The third part of JWT is signature which is used to verify that the sender of the JWT is  Loyverse and used to ensure that the message wasn’t changed along the way.
To verify signature you should use keys that you can get by calling `api.loyverse.com/.well-known/jwks.json` endpoint.
Response example:
```
{
  "keys":
  [
    {
      "kty":"RSA",
      "n": "0vx7agoebGcQSuuPiLJXZptN9nndrQmbXEps2aiAFbWhM78LhWx
  4cbbfAAtVT86zwu1RK7aPFFxuhDR1L6tSoc_BJECPebWKRXjBZCiFV4n3oknjhMs
  tn64tZ_2W-5JsGY4Hc5n9yBXArwl93lqt7_RN5w6Cf0h4QyQ5v-65YGjQR0_FDW2
  QvzqY368QQMicAtaSqzs8KJZgnYb9c7d0zgdAZHzu6qMQvRL5hajrn1n91CbOpbI
  SD08qNLyrdkt-bFTWhAI4vMQFh6WeZu0fM4lFd2NcRwr3XPksINHaQ-G_xBniIqb
  w0Ls1jF44-csFCur-kEgU8awapJzKnqDKgw",
      "e":"AQAB",
      "alg":"RS256",
      "kid":"2011-04-29"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Discovery document

The OpenID Connect protocol requires the use of multiple endpoints for authenticating users, and for requesting resources including tokens, user information, and public keys.
To simplify implementations and increase flexibility, OpenID Connect allows the use of a "Discovery document," a JSON document found at a well-known location containing key-value pairs which provide details about the OpenID Connect provider's configuration, including the URIs of the authorization, token, revocation, userinfo, and public-keys endpoints. The Discovery document for Loyverse OpenID Connect service may be found here:
```
https://api.loyverse.com/.well-known/openid-configuration
```
Response example:
```
{
  "issuer": "https://api.loyverse.com",
  "authorization_endpoint": "https://api.loyverse.com/oauth/authorize",
  "token_endpoint": "https://api.loyverse.com/oauth/token",
  "userinfo_endpoint": "https://api.loyverse.com/userinfo",
  "jwks_uri": "https://api.loyverse.com/.well-known/jwks.json",
  "scopes_supported": [
    "items_read",
    "items_write",
    "customers_read",
    "customers_write",
    "employees_read",
    "inventory_read",
    "inventory_write",
    "pos_devices_read",
    "pos_devices_write",
    "receipts_read",
    "receipts_write",
    "shifts_read",
    "stores_read",
    "payment_types_read",
    "taxes_read",
    "taxes_write",
    "merchant_read",
    "profile_read",
    "suppliers_read",
    "suppliers_write",
    "openid"
  ],
  "response_types_supported": [
    "code"
  ]
}
```







# Pagination 

Some API endpoints paginate their responses to make the result set easier to handle. For example, if you request a list of items that is potentially too large to handle efficiently, the endpoint will return the first batch of results along with a marker of some kind to access the next batch of results. You may be able to avoid dealing with pagination by narrowing your initial request. 

Paginated results include a cursor field as part of the response body. To fetch the next set of results, send a followup request to the same endpoint and provide the cursor value returned in the previous response as a query parameter. When the endpoint sends the final set of results, the response body will not include a cursor field.

It is possible to change the number of objects returned in the response. It can be done by passing the `limit` parameter. Default value is 50 and maximum is 250.



# API rate limits

The Loyverse API platform applies rate limits to the API requests that it receives. Every request is subject to throttling under our general limits. There are additional resource-based rate limits. Your app should be prepared to implement retry behavior if it is throttled.
The current limit is 300 requests per 300 sec per account. All requests that are made after rate limits have been exceeded are throttled and an HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` error is returned. 

# Date and time format
All dates and times in the API are in UTC. In requests you should specify dates and times in UTC. When processing responses you should convert dates and times to your local time.

# Soft deletion

Loyverse uses soft-deletion for most of its records. In the API, a soft-deleted object will have a special status. These records will not be returned by default, but can be accessed using `"show_deleted" = "true"` filter  and have `deleted_at` parameter. Notice that some resources (like customers) don't use soft deletion due to personal data restrictions.

# Handling errors

The API will return an Error List for a failed request, which will contain one or more Error objects.

```
{
  errors: [
    {
      code: "NOT_FOUND",
      details: "The resource was not found",
      field: "category_id"
    }
  ]
}
```
The Loyverse API uses the following error codes:

Error code|Description
----------|-------------
500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR | Generic internal server error. Try again later.
400 BAD_REQUEST | General client error. The request was not understood by the server, generally due to bad syntax.
400 INCORRECT_VALUE_TYPE | The JSON value type for the field is incorrect. For example, a string instead of an integer.
400 MISSING_REQUIRED_PARAMETER | A required path, query, or body parameter is missing.
400 INVALID_VALUE | A parameter's value is incorrect.
400 INVALID_RANGE | Specified time range is incorrect. For example, the end time is before the start time.
400 INVALID_CURSOR | The pagination cursor is incorrect.
400 CONFLICTING_PARAMETERS | 1 or more of the request parameters conflict with each other.
401 UNAUTHORIZED | An authentication error. Request had a missing, malformed, or invalid authorization data
402 PAYMENT_REQUIRED | The subscription of account has lapsed
403 FORBIDDEN | The resource requested is not available with your permissions
404 NOT_FOUND | The resource was not found
415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE | The server doesn't accept the submitted content-type.
429 RATE_LIMITED | The request was not accepted because the application has exceeded the rate limit.

# Webhooks overview

Webhooks are the best way to get real-time notifications about different events in Loyverse system. One way to be in sync with Loyverse updates is to periodically pull the particular endpoint, but webhooks give you more effective way to accomplish this task. 

Supported webhook events:

Event|Description
----------|-------------
inventory_levels.update |  Webhook is fired when a item’s inventory is updated.
items.update |  Webhook is fired when an item is created, updated or deleted.
customers.update |  Webhook is fired when a customer is created, updated or deleted.
receipts.update |  Webhook is fired when a receipt is created or updated.
shifts.create |   Webhook is fired when a closed shift is created.

When an event occurs, Loyverse collects data on the event, creates a notification, and sends it as a POST request to the notification URL registered while configuring  webhook.

## Adding webhook
There are two ways to configure webhooks:
* **Personal Access Token** — use the [/webhooks endpoint](https://developer.loyverse.com/docs/#tag/Webhooks) or the web interface at https://r.loyverse.com/dashboard/#/webhooks. Webhooks created this way belong to the merchant and are **not signed** — the `X-Loyverse-Signature` header is not included in their notifications.
* **OAuth2 application** — use the [/webhooks endpoint](https://developer.loyverse.com/docs/#tag/Webhooks) with an OAuth2 access token. Webhooks created this way are owned by the application and **are signed** — every notification includes an `X-Loyverse-Signature` header generated using the application's Client Secret.

You can subscribe to a single event in one webhook. The combination of event type and url must be unique. The specified URL must be formatted correctly, use the HTTPS, and be reachable.


## Webhook payload

Once you create a webhook, Loyverse will send a HTTP POST request to the URL defined by the webhook every time when event occurs. The POST request contain JSON data with details of the object that caused the hooked event and HTTP headers that provide context.

Payload example for `inventory_levels.update` event type:
```
{
  "merchant_id": "5fk4f446-01d2-8787-4fd5-7b7b1995df85",
  "type": "inventory_levels.update",
  "created_at": "2020-06-07T17:23:48.562Z",
  "inventory_levels": [
    {
      "variant_id": "5fk4f446-01d2-8787-4fd5-7b7b1995df85",
      "store_id": "5fk4f446-01d2-8787-4fd5-7b7b1995df85",
      "in_stock": 0,
      "updated_at": "2019-08-24T14:15:22Z"
    }
  ]
}

```


You will find additional HTTP headers for a request:

HTTP header|Description
----------|-------------
X-Loyverse-Signature | A signature used to validate the notification authenticity. **Only present for webhooks created by OAuth2 applications.** (See Validate notifications section for more information)
X-Loyverse-API-version | Used to confirm what version of the Loyverse API used to serialize the webhook payload (for example "v1.0")


If there is batch update of objects in the system (for example, caused by items import), Loyverse will send several request with maximum 100 objects in the array.

## Testing webhook

If you create a webhook via web interface, you can quickly test your configuration by sending test notification. Loyverse will send test POST request with the dummy data the specified URL.
When testing webhooks, you can run your server or use different services such as Beeceptor.


## Validate notifications

This section applies to **webhooks created by OAuth2 applications**. Webhooks created with a Personal Access Token do not include the `X-Loyverse-Signature` header and do not require signature validation.

Because your webhook endpoint is publicly accessible, anyone on the internet can send requests to it. To confirm that a notification genuinely came from Loyverse and was not tampered with in transit, you must verify the signature attached to every webhook request from an OAuth2-owned webhook.

**How the signature works**

Every webhook request from Loyverse includes an `X-Loyverse-Signature` header. Its value is a lowercase hex-encoded HMAC-SHA1 digest computed from the raw request body, using your application's **Client Secret** as the key.

**How to verify the signature**

Follow these steps each time your endpoint receives a webhook request:

1. **Read the raw request body.** Use the exact bytes received — do not parse, decode, or reformat the body before computing the digest.
2. **Retrieve your Client Secret.** This is the secret associated with your OAuth application in the Loyverse Developer Portal.
3. **Compute an HMAC-SHA1 digest.** Use your Client Secret (encoded as UTF-8) as the key and the raw request body (encoded as UTF-8) as the message.
4. **Hex-encode the result.** Convert each byte of the HMAC output to a two-character lowercase hexadecimal string and concatenate them.
5. **Compare the values.** Check that the hex-encoded digest you just computed matches the value in the `X-Loyverse-Signature` header of the incoming request. Use a constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks.

If the values match, the request is authentic. If they do not match, reject the request — do not process its payload.

## Request timeout and retries
When receiving webhook request on your end you must send a 2xx response. Any response outside of the 2xx range, will be considered by Loyverse as a delivery failure. Loyverse does not follow redirects for webhook notifications and considers them to be an error response.
In the case of delivery failure Loyverse will retry sending the request 200 times during 48 hours. If there is no 2XX response within this time range, then the webhook status will be changed to "Disabled". Loyverse will send a warning message to the developer email address.

post.description:
When using the refund API you should take into account these notes:
* At the moment refund API allows creating a refund only for sales receipts which are paid by a single payment. For any attempt to make a refund for a sales receipt that has more than one payment Loyverse API will respond with an error.
* Refund API doesn't support a refund of receipts paid by integrated payments using Loyverse POS app (e.g. iZettle, Sumup, etc.). For this purpose please use Loyverse POS app.
* If a refund is created successfully, it will cause a restock of items specified in a refund receipt.

id.description: The webhook id. Including this id in POST request will cause an update of existing webhook

id.description: The merchant id

country.description: The country code associated with the merchant account (ISO 3166-1-alpha-2 format)

decimal_places.description: The number of decimal places for the currency

employee_id.description: The employee id associated with the receipt

line_items.description: The line items included in the refund

variant_id.description: The variant id for inventory level update

stock_after.description: New stock value of the item variant

id.description: The pos device id. If included in the POST request it will cause an update instead of a creating a new object.

store_id.description: The store id this device is connected to

activated.description: Shows the status of the POS device. If true, this device is connected to the physical device.

store_id.description: The store id associated with the shift

pos_device_id.description: The pos device id associated with the shift

opened_at.description: The time when the shift was opened

closed_at.description: The time when the shift was closed

opened_by_employee.description: The employee id who opened the shift

closed_by_employee.description: The employee id who closed the shift

starting_cash.description: The initial money amount at the start of the shift

cash_payments.description: The total money amount of cash payments for the shift

cash_refunds.description: The total money amount of cash refunds for the shift

paid_in.description: The money amount added to the cash drawer.

paid_out.description: The money amount removed from the cash drawer. The value is always positive.

expected_cash.description: The expected money amount at the end of the shift

actual_cash.description: The actual money amount at the end of the shift

gross_sales.description: The gross money amount for the shift. It calculates as sum of all payments before discounts but after taxes with type INCLUDED.

refunds.description: The total money amount of refunds for the shift

discounts.description: The total money amount of discounts for the shift. The value is always positive.

net_sales.description: The net money amount for the shift. It calculates as gross sales minus discounts and refunds

tip.description: The total money amount of tips for the shift. Tips are available only for some payment types.

surcharge.description: The total money amount of surcharge for the shift. Surcharge is available only for some payment types.

taxes.description: The list of taxes and it's totals for the shift

money_amount.description: The total money amount for the tax in the shift

payments.description: The list of total money amounts for every payment type in the shift

money_amount.description: The total money amount for the payment type

cash_movements.description: The list of shift cash movements

money_amount.description: The money amount. The value is always positive.

comment.description: The description of the cash movement

employee_id.description: The employee id who made the cash movement

created_at.description: The time when this cash movement was created (ISO 8601 format, e.g. 2020-03-25T19:55:23.077Z)

stores.description: The list of store ids where this employee has access

id.description: The supplier id. If included in the POST request it will cause an update instead of a creating a new object.

city.description: The supplier city, town, or village.

region.description: The supplier’s region name. Typically a province, a state, or a prefecture.

postal_code.description: The supplier’s postal code, also known as zip, postcode, Eircode, etc.

country_code.description: The two-letter country code corresponding to the supplier country in ISO 3166-1-alpha-2 format.

id.description: The customer id. If included in the POST request it will cause an update instead of a creating a new object.

postal_code.description: The customer’s postal code, also known as zip, postcode, Eircode, etc.

first_visit.description: The date of the first customer visit

last_visit.description: The date of the most recent customer visit

total_spent.description: The total money amount that customer had spent

id.description: The tax id. If included in the POST request it will cause an update instead of a creating a new object.

type.description: If the type is `INCLUDED` then the tax is included in an item price. If the type is `ADDED` then the tax is added to an item price

rate.description: The tax rate. For example, a value of "5.255" corresponds to a percentage of 5.255%

stores.description: The list of store ids where this tax is available

discount_amount.description: The discount value in money representation (only for discounts with type FIXED_AMOUNT)

discount_percent.description: This is discount value in percentage (only for discounts with type FIXED_PERCENT)

restricted_access.description: If true, the password verification is necessary in order to apply this discount on POS.

in_stock.description: The current stock at the specified store

updated_at.description: The time when specified stock was calculated

id.description: Read-only internal id of the item. If included in the POST request it will cause an update instead of a creating a new object.

reference_id.description: External reference id for the item

category_id.description: The category id of the item

track_stock.description: If true, the system tracks inventory for this item at all stores. Make sure you don't accidentally disable track stock. If you set `track_stock` to false then all inventory levels of this item are set to 0

sold_by_weight.description: If true, a fractional quantity for this item can be specified at the time of a sale (for example 1.5)

is_composite.description: If true, the item contains a specified quantity of other items. [Learn more](https://help.loyverse.com/help/how-create-composite-item)

use_production.description: If true, the system tracks stock not only for its components but also for this item. This property can be set only for composite items. [Learn more](https://help.loyverse.com/help/how-work-production)

components.description: The list of components for the item. [Learn more](https://help.loyverse.com/help/how-create-composite-item)

tax_ids.description: The list of tax ids applied to this item

modifiers_ids.description: The list of modifiers ids applied to this item

form.description: The visual form of the item that is displayed on the POS

color.description: One of the predefined colors for the item that is displayed on the POS

option1_name.description: The name of the first option (for example "Size"). [Learn more](https://help.loyverse.com/help/how-use-variants-items)

option2_name.description: The name of the first option (for example "Color"). [Learn more](https://help.loyverse.com/help/how-use-variants-items)

option3_name.description: The name of the first option (for example "Material"). [Learn more](https://help.loyverse.com/help/how-use-variants-items)

variant_id.description: The read only internal id of the variant.
The read only internal id of the variant. If included in the POST request it will cause an update instead of a creating a new object.

item_id.description: The item id this variant is attached to.

sku.description: The variant sku. It should be unique.

reference_variant_id.description: External reference id for the variant

option1_value.description: The value of the first option for this variant. Required if option1_name is set for the item this variant is attached to.

option2_value.description: The value of the second option for this variant. Required if option2_name is set for the item this variant is attached to.

option3_value.description: The value of the third option for this variant. Required if option3_name is set for the item this variant is attached to.

default_pricing_type.description: The default variant pricing type. If the value is `VARIABLE` than the price is specified at the time of a sale. If there are several stores in the account than the price of the variant in each store is equal to this value by default unless different value is specified in the `stores` array for a particular store.

default_price.description: The default variant price (only for `pricing_type: FIXED`) If there are several stores in the account than the price of the variant in each store is equal to this value by default unless different value is specified in the `stores` array for a particular store.

stores.description: The list of values that are unique for each store

created_at.description: The time when this resource was created

updated_at.description: The time when this resource was created

deleted_at.description: The time when this resource was created

pricing_type.description: The variant pricing type. If the value is `VARIABLE` than the price is specified at the time of a sale. The value is equal to `default_pricing_type` by default

price.description: The variant price in this store (only if pricing_type in this store is `FIXED`). The value is equal to `default_price` by default

available_for_sale.description: If true, variant is available for sale at this store

optimal_stock.description: The variant optimal stock. This value is used to automatically calculate stock while creating purchase order. [Learn more](https://help.loyverse.com/help/autofill-items-purchase-order)

low_stock.description: The low stock threshold for the variant. If the variant stock is equal or below this threshold, the system shows alert in the back-office and sends email (if enabled). [Learn more](https://help.loyverse.com/help/low-stocks)

store_id.description: The store id associated with the receipt

employee_id.description: The employee id associated with the receipt

order.description: The order name or number associated with the receipt

customer_id.description: The customer id associated with the receipt

source.description: The name of the the source this receipt comes from. By default it is the name of the application that created the receipt. For receipts created from Loyverse mobile point of sale application the value is "point of sale".

receipt_date.description: By default, it matches the created_at value. You can set receipt_date to the date and time in the past when the receipt was created in another system. This value is used in Loyverse back-office reports.

total_discounts.description: The list of all discounts applied in the receipt. Discounts can be applied in two scopes, RECEIPT or LINE_ITEM. For discount with LINE_ITEM level you must reference to corresponding discount in every line item where this discount is applied. For discounts with RECEIPT level, line_discount for every line item will be generated automatically.

line_items.description: The line items included in the receipt

payments.description: The list of payments. There is a restriction that only one payment can be applied to receipt when using POST request.

id.description: The id of existing discount

scope.description: The level for applying discount. If value is `RECEIPT` than `line_discount` is calculated for every line_item and you don't have to reference this discount in every line_item. If value is `LINE_ITEM` than the discount applies only for line items with a discount reference in their `line_discounts` field.

percentage.description: The percentage of the discount. For example value 10.55 corresponds to a percentage of 10.55%. Set this value only for discount with type `VARIABLE_PERCENTAGE`

money_amount.description: The money amount of the discount. Set this value only for discount with type `VARIABLE_AMOUNT` and `DISCOUNT_BY_POINTS`

id.description: The id of existing tax

uid.description: Unique id that identifies the tax only within this request. You can use this id for referencing this tax in `line_items`

variant_id.description: The variant id for this line item

quantity.description: The number of items that were purchased (or refunded in case of refund)

price.description: The price of one item. It includes taxes which type is INCLUDED. It doesn't include discounts, modifiers and taxes which type is ADDED. By default it is equal to the price of the item variant with specified variant_id.

cost.description: The cost of one item at the moment of transaction. By default it is equal to the cost of the item variant with specified variant_id.

line_taxes.description: The list of taxes applied to the line item

line_discounts.description: The list of discounts applied to the line item

line_modifiers.description: The list of modifiers applied to the line item
